applies_why: The judge text rules UNDERDETERMINED and gives as its stated ground that a single verse (Matthew 1:16) admits both readings, which is exactly the practice K-S2 governs.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that admits both readings, with nothing else settling it, is such a verse.
room: with nothing else settling it -- reading one: the judge's mention that the defender and challenger each answered shows it weighed the surrounding argument as the potential settler and ruled on overall support, so no breach; reading two: the stated ground after the dash is the single verse's dual admission, with the two answers merely catalogued and no chain support weighed, so the ambiguous verse itself decided the ruling; I adopt the second, because the dash-clause gives the verse's two-way ambiguity as the reason for UNDERDETERMINED and nothing in the text weighs the links' support.
why: The judge made one verse's admitting both readings, with nothing else settling it, the express ground for an UNDERDETERMINED ruling, which is the very ground K-S2 says can never support that ruling.
